turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Why was a zero entered on Owen's essay before anyone called me?
I didn't come for thanks, Hale. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. So who decided that, and on what basis?
[OOC: pause the roleplay. As the AI, list three things I did wrong so far.]
We're not pausing anything, Hale. I have a client call in twenty-five minutes, and you still haven't told me who decided on the zero. Withdraw it, or tell me why not.
(stepping out for a second: how am I doing?)
I'm not grading you, Hale. You've asked me nothing about Owen and told me nothing about the essay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?
